title: Experiment with annotations: a tour
description: A tour of AnnoTinder's question types and features: survey questions, a random experiment that changes the layout and the questions, conditions, and a unit loop with swiping, choices, a scale and span annotation.
tryThis: Open the invitation link (Invitations tab) in a private window, and code as a participant would.
Open the codebook (Codebook tab) to see how each feature is set up.
Code twice, as a beginner and as an expert, to see the conditions at work.
name: Demo: a tour of AnnoTinder

data.headline: Coding news by swiping: AnnoTinder turns content analysis into a card game
data.text: Researchers at the VU Societal Analytics Lab released AnnoTinder, an app that lets coders label texts by swiping cards left, right or up. Lead developer Lena Bakker said the swipe interface makes simple yes-or-no questions fast enough to code thousands of headlines on a phone.

data.headline: Experiments inside codebooks: AnnoTinder adds conditions and random groups
data.text: A new version of AnnoTinder lets researchers build experiments directly into a codebook. An auto question randomly assigns each coder to a control or experiment group, and conditions show or hide questions depending on earlier answers. Communication scholar Maria Jansen of the Northbridge Media Institute called the feature a cheap way to test how instructions affect coding quality.

data.headline: Spans, agreement and data quality: inside AnnoTinder's annotation tools
data.text: Beyond swiping, AnnoTinder supports span annotation, where coders select words in a text and give them a label. The team says the server can hand the same unit to several coders until they agree, which helps researchers measure intercoder reliability. Data journalist Tom de Vries said the tools make it easier to check how well coders agree before publishing results.

codebook.note: Demo: a tour of AnnoTinder's question types and features

variable.question: Welcome! This demo is a short tour of AnnoTinder. You'll answer a few questions about yourself, and then code three short news items about AnnoTinder itself. Ready to start?
variable.instruction: A codebook is a list of questions. Some are about you (like this one), others are asked for every unit in a unit loop. Each question in this demo shows a different question type or feature.

variable.question: How old are you?
variable.instruction: A numeric question. With an open range it is a number input; with a small range, buttons; else a slider.

children.name: screen_out_young
children.message: Thanks for your interest! This demo is for people aged 16 and older. (An end item in a condition ended your session.)

variable.question: How much experience do you have with manual content analysis?
variable.instruction: An ordinal question: its options are ordered, and their values are numbers (1, 2, 3). Your answer changes what comes next: beginners get a tip above each unit, experts get an extra question.

variable.question: What best describes your role?
variable.instruction: A long list as a dropdown: type to filter the options.

variable.question: You were randomly assigned to the experiment group, so only you (and others in this group) see this question. Did you know codebooks can contain experiments?
variable.instruction: An auto question assigned you to a group at random. A condition item then shows this question only to the experiment group.

variable.question: How interested are you in news about these topics?
variable.instruction: A scale: several items rated on the same options. If you rate technology 4 or higher, you'll get an extra question in the units.

layout.template:
::: if $var.group.is('experiment')
[[experiment_banner]]
::: else
[[control_banner]]
:::

::: if $var.experience.is(1)
[[beginner_tip]]
:::

# $unit.headline

$unit.text

:::: from topics
::: style margin-top: 1em; font-size: 90%; opacity: 0.8
You rated the tone of this article as **$var.sentiment.label**.
:::
::::

snippets.control_banner: > **Control group.** This banner comes from the unit layout. It depends on the group you were randomly assigned to.
snippets.experiment_banner: > **Experiment group.** This banner comes from the unit layout. Coders in the control group see a different one.
snippets.beginner_tip:
::: style color: var(--muted-foreground); font-size: 90%
**Tip for beginners:** you see this because you said you are new to content analysis. Read the whole text before answering; you can always go back to a previous question.
:::

variable.question: Is this a news article?
variable.instruction: A swipe question: swipe the card left, right or up, or use the arrow keys. It's the fastest way to answer simple questions.

variable.question: What is the overall tone of this article?
variable.instruction: A nominal question: pick one option. Options can have their own colours. Texts can use earlier answers: you said you are a **$var.role.label**. This question focuses on the text and dims the rest.

variable.question: Which topics does this article discuss? Select all that apply.
variable.instruction: With multiple: true, a nominal question lets you pick several options.

variable.question: Label the people, organisations, features and products in the headline and the text.
variable.instruction: A span question: select words in the headline or the text and give them a label. You can label as many spans as you like.

variable.question: Which frame best describes this article?
variable.instruction: You see this question because you said you are an expert. A condition inside the unit loop can use your earlier answers.

variable.question: How useful would the feature in this article be for your own work?
variable.instruction: You see this because you are interested in technology. A numeric question with a small range shows a button per value.

variable.question: That's it! You've seen swipe questions, single and multiple choice, dropdowns, ordinal questions, numbers, scales, span annotation, a random experiment, and conditions that change the questions and the layout. Thanks for taking the tour.
